summary: Amy Heller is a scholar in tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Barnard College, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald, she held posts at Yale University (1982) and the CNRS (attested 2005).

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~2002-2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014).

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar of tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Virginia, completing her PhD under David Germano in 2004, alongside studies under numerous traditional and academic teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a specialist in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993) and held a post at the University of Washington (~1995).

Ana Agud is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Salamanca (~1965-1974) and the University of Tübingen (~1970-1973). She served as a professor in classical and Indo-European philology at Salamanca (~1986-2018).

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864-1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya and Royal College, Colombo (~1878-1883), he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891.

Anagarika Govinda (1898-1985) worked in Buddhist studies and tibetology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Freiburg, studied under Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, taught at Patna University (~1935-1936), and served as Ācārya at Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933-1985).
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and has served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Ananda Coomaraswamy (1877-1947) was a scholar of Indology, history/archaeology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London (~1897-1900), he held posts at the Smithsonian Institution and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1917-1947).

Ananda W. P. Guruge (1928-2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Ceylon and University of London. He held posts at NIEPA (~1968-1972) and the University of the West (~2005-2014).

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898-1959) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1930-1949), Patna University (~1949-1959), and served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (~1950-1959).

Anantalal Thakur (1916-2009) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Mithila Research Institute (~1955-1974) and as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (1968-1971).
Ananya Jahanara Kabir is a scholar of Indology. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1993-1997) and held a post at King's College London (~2013).

Andrea Acri is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, worked there as a researcher (~2006-2011), and joined EPHE in 2016.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University, later becoming an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis.
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed her Master's degree (2008) and PhD (2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and tibetology. He studied under several traditional Rinpoches and earned a PhD from the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura.
Andree Dominique Messent is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, having also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov (1904-1937) was a scholar of tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky).
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
